summary: Teutamides (Ancient Greek Τευταμίδης) was a king of Larissa in Thessaly in whose father's funeral games Perseus accidentally killed Acrisius with a discus, fulfilling the oracle that Danaë's son would slay her father. The atlas keeps him distinct from Homeric Teutamus, grandfather of the Pelasgian captains at Troy.
etymology: Teutamidēs is a patronymic formation; ancient authors sometimes write Teutamus / Teutamias for related Larissan figures.

sections.heading: Funeral games and Acrisius
paragraphs: Apollodorus (Bibliotheca 2.4.4) sets the death of Acrisius at athletic games held in Larissa. Perseus' quoit strikes his grandfather's foot; the wound kills the Argive king and closes the oracle that had driven Danaë and the infant into exile.
Wikipedia's Teutamides stub also folds in Hellanicus' Amyntorid genealogy and Homeric Lethus — material the atlas assigns carefully across nodes.

sections.heading: Homonyms
paragraphs: This node (teutamides-larissa) is the Larissan king of the Perseus episode. He is not Teutamus father of Pelasgian Lethus in Homer's Trojan catalogue (teutamus-pelasgian), nor the historical Macedonian officer Teutamus.
